clue.text: Joined diplomat on date

parts.note: an attaché is a junior diplomat on an embassy staff

explanation.surface: Someone joined a diplomat on a romantic date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the date after the diplomat in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fastened or connected to another thing is joined to it, both past participles.

clue.text: One, out of condition, losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the word unfit is dropped

parts.note: someone out of condition is unfit, not in good physical shape

explanation.surface: Someone out of shape loses their enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes F, the middle letter of UNFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single whole, the quantity one in counting.

clue.text: Who can operate this time machine?!

definitions.text: Who can operate this time machine?!

parts.words: Who can operate this time machine?!
parts.note: Who is the time-travelling Doctor of the BBC series, whose police-box craft only he can pilot, not a question word

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about who knows how to work a time machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Who' as Doctor Who, the long-running British TV science-fiction series; his time machine looks like a blue police box.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doctor's craft in the British science-fiction show is the famous time-travelling vessel.

clue.text: Best final

definitions.meaning: best here means supreme, the greatest example of its kind
final means last, coming at the very end

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the supreme or greatest example and the last in a series.

clue.text: More plots developed surrounding one big city

indicators.note: surrounding means the rearranged letters are placed around the letter for one
developed means the letters of more plots are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A novelist develops further plots set in a sprawling city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns MOREPLOTS into METROPOLS, and 'surrounding' has that placed round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large urban centre, often a capital or chief city.

clue.text: Scottish boy in English club keeled over drinking drop of rum

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round
keeled over means toppled, so the pair of English and club is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club

indicators.note: drop of means just the first letter of the word rum is taken

explanation.surface: A Scottish lad at an English club falls over after drinking rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeled over' turns E + IRON into NORIE, and 'drinking' puts R (the first letter of 'rum', from 'drop of') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Norrie is a Scottish pet form of the male name Norman.

clue.text: Usual quality

definitions.meaning: usual here means normal or customary, as in the regular model
quality here means a level of excellence, as in a high bar to meet

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both normal or customary and a level of excellence to be met.

clue.text: Coercion of the French on steamship

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'
re means on or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: A French passenger complains of being forced aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is pressure or threats used to force someone to act against their will.

clue.text: Avoid attention of one group in outskirts of Ludlow

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the outer letters of the town name
outskirts of means only the first and last letters of the word Ludlow are used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a rock band

explanation.surface: A fugitive keeps a low profile among a gang on the edge of Ludlow.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludlow is a small market town in Shropshire, England; its first and last letters L and W enclose I + ELO.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for keeping out of sight and not drawing notice.

clue.text: Long or short trousers

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the word for trousers

parts.note: pants is the American word for trousers

explanation.surface: A choice between long or short trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here, as in to pant for or yearn; 'short' docks the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant for something is to yearn or crave it, as the verb long does.

clue.text: Dior's the last word in fashion?

definitions.text: Dior's the last word in fashion?

parts.words: Dior's the last word in fashion?
parts.note: a French couturier would naturally use French for the latest style, a phrase literally meaning last cry

explanation.surface: Is Dior the final authority on what is fashionable?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is French, borrowed into English; Dior is a Paris fashion house, hinting at the language.
explanation.definitionFit: The French borrowing means the newest trend or very latest style.

clue.text: Monkey in rushes, camouflaged

indicators.note: camouflaged means the letters of rushes are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A monkey hides itself among the rushes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a South Asian monkey widely used in research.

clue.text: Presley record Yukon scout ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of Yukon scout are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scout in the Yukon orders an Elvis disc.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1960 Elvis Presley hit single was a chart-topping record.

clue.text: Rascal's uneasy sleep (nap)

indicators.note: uneasy means the letters of sleep and nap are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue's sleep is troubled, so he takes a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Rascal's' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay. A spalpeen is an Irish term for a scamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Spalpeen is an Irish word for a scamp or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Puts off daughter and other relatives

parts.note: aunts are relatives other than a daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter and her aunts postpone a family visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To daunt someone is to discourage or intimidate them, a verb in the same form.

clue.text: Knight's vehicle outside topless joint

indicators.note: outside means the vehicle's letters go around the trimmed joint

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word for joint is removed in this down clue

parts.note: the wrist is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: A knight's car is parked outside a disreputable topless bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Knight's' stands for 'is'. 'topless' leaves RIST; 'outside' wraps the vehicle round it. 'topless joint' tempts as a seedy bar, but the joint is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tristram is a knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Rise to the surface nicely ahead

parts.note: nicely means well, in a pleasing manner
up means ahead, as in a team being up on points

explanation.surface: Something bobs to the top neatly and in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or tears welling up surge upward from below, an idiom for emerging.

clue.text: Grim reaper hanging around church for clergyman

indicators.note: hanging around means the scrambled letters loiter round the abbreviation for church
grim means the letters of reaper are rendered into a dire mixed-up form

explanation.surface: Death lingers near a church, waiting for a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grim Reaper is the robed figure of death, so 'Grim' hides as part of a familiar phrase while signalling the anagram PREAER; 'hanging around' then wraps that round the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher delivers sermons, a minister or cleric.

clue.text: Trainspotter, a girl close to track

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word track is taken

explanation.surface: A girl stands near the railway line, notebook in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an anorak is slang for an obsessive enthusiast of a dull hobby, such as noting train numbers, after the waterproof jacket they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an obsessive hobbyist, with the trainspotter the classic example.

clue.text: Port and raki drunk by celebrity

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of raki are tipsy and jumbled

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: A celebrity drinks raki in a Greek harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Raki is an anise spirit from Greece and Turkey; 'drunk' makes IRAK, and 'by' sets the celebrity beside it. The port is better known today as Heraklion, on Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cretan city, also spelt Heraklion, is a major seaport.

clue.text: Went on horseback round hot southern island

indicators.note: round means the riding word goes about the letter for hot

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride, to go on horseback
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A rider tours a hot southern island on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek isle in the Aegean Sea, largest of the Dodecanese.

clue.text: A group of six tsetse flies

indicators.note: flies is a verb here: the letters of tsetse fly apart and reassemble

explanation.surface: Half a dozen tsetse flies buzz about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' reads as the insect noun but works as a verb signalling rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a set of six, especially the last six lines of a sonnet.

clue.text: Change models? Not very often

indicators.note: change means the letters of models are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion house rarely swaps its models.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, an adverb meaning infrequently.

clue.text: Forced on regular after noon

indicators.note: after means the pieces on and regular follow the letter for noon

parts.note: taken as written
natural means regular or normal

explanation.surface: Someone was compelled to visit a regular customer in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contrived or strained is unnatural rather than spontaneous.

clue.text: Runs against one in sprint

indicators.note: against means beside or next to, putting the letter for runs alongside the one

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: An athlete competes against a rival in a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest of speed, a dash or short fast run.

clue.text: Widespread fire out of control

indicators.note: out of control means the letters of fire run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A blaze out of control spreads everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Rife means prevalent or occurring everywhere, especially of something bad.

clue.text: Some villager on about a Spanish city

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A local talks about a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run of letters lying across villaGER ON About.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerona, now usually Girona, is a Catalan city in northeast Spain.

clue.text: Plonker out of order about female guitarist

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the letter for female
out of order means the letters of Plonker are rearranged

parts.note: plonker is British slang for a fool, used here only as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fool behaving badly is rude about a woman guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' turns PLONKER into KNOPLER, and 'about' puts it round F. Plonker is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Knopfler is the lead guitarist of the rock band Dire Straits.
